features.method: OpenStreetMap way 1563711916 (man_made=observatory, name='HAWC Gamma-Ray Observatory'), a closed 16-node polygon used verbatim. It encloses the tank field and its surroundings (32,500 m2, about 45 % more than the 22,395 m2 platform), so it is a mapper's outline of the observatory site and is not compared with the platform area.
features.name: HAWC Gamma-Ray Observatory (OpenStreetMap observatory polygon)

provenance.note: Single-version polygon created 2026-09-30; no official figure to check against.

features.method: Convex hull (Andrew's monotone chain on lon/lat) of every vertex of the 300 OpenStreetMap tank polygons (see geometry:hawc-tanks), 33 vertices. A hull encloses the gaps between rows and the counting-house gap, so it is the outline the tank field presents, not a boundary or fence. The paper's own area figures for the array (22,000 m2) and for the levelled platform (22,395 m2) are compared with its area.
features.name: HAWC tank field outline (convex hull of the 300 tanks)

provenance.locator: convex hull of the vertices of OSM ways 541455344..541455690 (extract 2026-10-25T10:38:54Z); HAWC ICRC 2013 contributions
provenance.note: Confidence 'derived' per contract: a derived shape is derived, even with passing checks. The 22,000, 22,500 and 22,395 m2 figures all appear in the HAWC ICRC 2013 contributions for the array or the platform.
provenance.quote: HAWC is composed of 300 water Cherenkov detectors built over an area of 22,000 m2

features.method: Union as one MultiPolygon, in way-id order and verbatim (13-node closed polygons, no simplification), of the 300 OpenStreetMap ways tagged building=storage_tank, man_made=storage_tank, content=water, height=5 (ids 541455344 to 541455690), which were traced as one set in 2017 and number exactly the 300 tanks of the array. Each polygon encloses 43.8 m2 against 41.9 m2 for a 7.3 m circle (an equivalent-circle diameter of 7.47 m, longest chord 7.65 m), i.e. the mappers drew each tank about 2 % wider than its nominal diameter; that over-size is the +4.7 % in the area check below. The 5 m height tag agrees with the published 5 m tank height.
features.name: HAWC water Cherenkov detector tanks (300 footprints)

provenance.note: OpenStreetMap tracing (rank 11), so confidence is capped at approximate even though the area check passes. The area check is on the sum of the 300 polygons against 300 circles of the published diameter.
provenance.quote: Each tank is a cylinder of 7.3m in diameter and 5m in height filled with water

summary.plain: The HAWC water-Cherenkov gamma-ray observatory of 300 water tanks on the Sierra Negra volcano, Puebla, Mexico, drawn tank by tank.
